reason: The cited evidence does not address FCC/BCC interfaces in HEA coatings. E1 discusses misfit and diffusion in γ/γ′ systems, not dislocation pinning by semi-coherent interfaces. E2 reports on dislocation climb and precipitation in a single-phase FCC HEA, with no mention of FCC/BCC interfaces. The key premises about interface-governed creep are therefore unsupported by the provided passages.
premises: Semi-coherent FCC/BCC interfaces act as strong pinning points for dislocations
High density of such interfaces retards stress-assisted dislocation climb
Reducing interface density/coherency increases creep strain rate
Reducing interface density/coherency lowers apparent activation energy for creep
Interface pinning dominates creep resistance at 500–600°C and moderate/high stresses
